shortName: University of Miami Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
Accepted coursework must be taken at a fully accredited U.S., U.S. territorial, or Canadian postsecondary institution. Science coursework must be completed at a 4-year (bachelor’s degree-granting) institution as described above. Community College coursework will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis as it applies to upward transfer pathways and accelerated enrollment. 

We accept Advanced Placement (AP) credits to satisfy English/literature, behavioral science, biology, physics, and inorganic chemistry requirements if these credits are verified by the American Medical School Application Service® (AMCAS) and appear on your college transcript. 

Accepted students are strongly encouraged to complete extensive coursework in the natural sciences, including: Cell & molecular biology, Computer science, Developmental Biology, Genetics, Immunology, Microbiology, Neuroscience, Physiology

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The school sponsors a special seven-week summer program that provides pre-medical undergraduates with opportunities to gain first-hand knowledge of the requirements of a medical education. Applications and information may be obtained by calling 305 243 5998.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may request a voluntary leave of absence from the UMMSM for educational, health-related, or other reasons. A request for leave of absence must be submitted in writing to the Office of Student Affairs using voluntary LOA form. Approval for a voluntary leave of absence must be granted by the Senior Associate Dean for Undergraduate Medical Education, in consultation with the Associate Dean for Student Affairs, the Associate Dean for Student Services and/or the Associate Regional Dean for Student Affairs.  In certain cases, a promotions committee may grant a voluntary leave of absence for academic or personal reasons.  Approval for the leave of absence will be provided in writing to the student, and will include the start date, anticipated date of return, and deadline by which a student should notify the medical education administration of his/her intent to resume their medical education. The medical education administration reserves the right not to approve a request for a volunt
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students at the Miller School of Medicine engage in a variety of activities with ample opportunities for leadership, service, and volunteerism. The UMMSM is deeply committed to service learning, and all levels of leadership and administration within the school support our student commitment to service.   Student organizations are registered through the Student Government, which currently oversees over 50 student-led groups. Students lead and participate in a variety of endeavors that enhance their learning outside the classroom. The spectrum of activities ranges from specialty-specific interest groups to community-based teaching programs, service to the local populations of Miami-Dade County, and multiple international medical mission trips. There is a high level of student participation in and satisfaction with extracurricular activities.   Peer teaching and service learning organizations are extremely important to UMMSM students.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine, the UM Hospitals and Clinics, Jackson Memorial Hospital, and the Miami VA are all located on the same campus at the heart of the Miami Health District, located in the Civic Center between Miami International Airport and Downtown. The Regional Medical Campus is located in Broward and Palm Beach counties, principally at Holy Cross Hospital, JFK Medical Center, and the Florida Department of Health in Palm Beach.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Approximately 65% of the class lives in an area approximately 5 miles from the UM medical campus in an area called Brickell. Approximately 20% of the class lives on Miami Beach. Some medical students live in apartment buildings adjacent to campus. The medical campus is served by Metrorail, an elevated light railway, which has made large areas of Miami including Brickell accessible to medical students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: A support system for gender and sexual minority students is available jointly through the Office of Student Services and the Office of Belonging & Inclusive Excellence.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: UMMSM recognizes the importance of promoting health and wellness resources to ensure our medical students can better achieve their educational and personal goals. We understand that being healthy and taking care of well-being helps students to be more productive and satisfied.  More info: https://med.miami.edu/medical-education/student-affairs/student-services/wellness-resources
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The diversity of our faculty and medical students increasingly mirrors that of our patient population. We serve a community that represents the future demographics of the U.S. population. Our brilliant clinicians and researchers are well-positioned to deliver outstanding clinical care and effectively address some of the most vexing challenges facing the medical profession.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: The Miller School of Medicine is within walking distance of accessible public transportation systems including bus and rail.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Medical students are expected to convey a professional demeanor with their behavior, dress and appearance.  A professional image increases credibility, trust, respect and confidence.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Student Services has two full-time academic enrichment specialists to confidentially assist students. In addition, there is a robust peer-tutoring program through the Academic Societies.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interactions begin early in the first year of medical school and continue throughout all four years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group problem-based learning, case-based learning, team-based learning, instructional videos aligned with self-assessment exercises, interactive sessions, simulations, and interactive lectures.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations:
Clinical rotations begin in the second year. 
Refer to curriculum for more information: https://med.miami.edu/medical-education/curriculum

medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance at all small group sessions and experiential clinical training is mandatory.  Attendance at lectures is highly encouraged but not mandatory; lectures are recorded and archived online daily.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
https://med.miami.edu/en/medical-education/curriculum/curriculum-phases

The curriculum is a program that integrates basic, clinical, and health systems sciences and requires students to be active and responsible learners. It emphasizes faculty and student-led team-based and small-group experiences wherein basic science concepts are introduced and assimilated in light of common disease states and clinical relevance. It also includes health systems science with an emphasis on social determinants of health, professionalism, humanism and ethics, population medicine, prevention and screening, quality and outcome assessment, medical informatics, geriatrics, integrative medicine, nutrition, health care economics, and end-of-life care. An over-arching theme throughout all four years is the continuous acquisition and refinement of clinical skills through expert teaching and patient encounters, starting in the first weeks of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The educational mission of the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine (UMMSM) is to graduate physicians with the ability and desire to improve the health of all populations by alleviating suffering and eliminating healthcare disparities through their leadership in patient care, research, education, health care administration and the community. The UMMSM has a number of programs and initiatives to promote primary care within its undergraduate medical programs.  From the first year of medical school, students have clinical experiences side by side with physicians. Our highly acclaimed Wolfson Department of Community Service (DOCS), an award-winning student-directed organization, provides preventive, primary, and subspecialty health care to medically underserved communities throughout Miami-Dade, Broward and Monroe Counties through ten community health fairs and four weekly student clinics.  Virtually all UMMSM students participate in DOCS programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students have the opportunity to work with faculty researchers on a wide range of research projects throughout their medical school years.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Wolfson DOCS, the Department of Community Service, conducts ten annual health fairs and four weekly clinics ( https://umdocs.mededu.miami.edu/ ).  There are also several global health experiences.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of Miami Miller School of Medicine is the largest and oldest medical school in the state of Florida. Six hospitals containing nearly 3,000 beds are located on the medical campus and provide a complete spectrum of clinical experiences. Specialty centers at the Miller School of Medicine include The Bascom Palmer Eye Institute and Anne Bates Leach Eye Hospital, the Ambulatory Care Center, the Diabetes Research Institute, the Lois Pope Life Center (which houses The Miami Project to Cure Spinal Cord Paralysis), the Bachelor Children's Research Institute, the Ryder Trauma Center, and the Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The University of Miami Miller School of Medicine’s mission is to provide state-of-the-art, translational and evidence-based information to enhance the quality of education, research, and clinical practice, to foster professional growth, to stimulate intellectual (academic) curiosity, and to promote excellence in the delivery of health care in South Florida and internationally. These educational activities will be relevant to medical knowledge, clinical performance, soundly performed research and/or patient outcomes.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The Medical Scholars Program (MSP), is specifically designed to provide exceptionally capable University of Miami undergraduate students with a pathway to early matriculation or early assurance into the Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine.

Students apply to the program early in their undergraduate career and are evaluated for conditional acceptance to the Leonard M. Miller School of Medicine. Students must engage in their undergraduate study and meet all conditions of the program throughout their enrollment at the University of Miami, for full acceptance and timely matriculation to the Miller School of Medicine.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
All letters of recommendation should be submitted through AMCAS. The Admissions Committee requires either a letter of evaluation from the premedical advisory committee at your school, or three letters from individuals who can speak to your strengths as a prospective medical student. Two of these letters should be from faculty members who have taught you in science coursework and can provide an evaluation both of your academic ability and of your personal qualifications for a career in medicine. Individual faculty members should also indicate in what capacity they have known you, for how long they have known you, and how well they know you. It is also helpful if they describe how you compare with other candidates for whom they have written letters.

Review the AMCAS Applicant Guide for more resources regarding letter of recommendation.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
REQUIRED:
-School Pre-Med Advisory Committee letter packet
OR
-3 letters from individuals who can speak to your strengths as a prospective medical student. Two of these letters should be from faculty members who have taught you in science coursework.

OPTIONAL:
Up to 3 additional letters from individuals who can speak to your strengths as a prospective medical student who you have worked with through your clinical experiences, research, community service, employment, or leadership activities.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Evaluation interviews conducted virtually by members of the Admissions Committee is an integral part of our selection process. Interviews are conducted only at the request of the Office of Admissions and are generally held on selected Mondays and Fridays between the middle of September and the end of April. 

The Committee gives careful consideration to many factors when evaluating candidates for admission. Some of these factors are:

Academic and behavioral preparedness to study medicine 
Breadth of life experiences 
Preparedness to serve diverse populations
Demonstrated interest in and experiences in direct patient care, research, and health care delivery
Interpersonal skill level 
Source and degree of motivation 
Maturity
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two 50-minute interviews: One open-file, experiential, one closed-file, behavioral.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews are being conducted virtually.  Beginning in November, we will offer on-site tours each month for accepted candidates.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The Admissions Committee establishes the Waitlist order.  The Associate Dean for Admissions and Enrollment has the authority to select from the Waitlist.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: The required and recommended courses were developed in consultation with Miller curriculum experts based on the academic pathways of previous students who were successful in Miller’s rigorous curriculum. There are broad ranges of topics covered in undergraduate coursework, naming conventions of courses, plans of study and credit hours, and other details that may make it challenging to determine if you have met our requirements. We're not able to conduct application reviews, including reviewing transcripts and other course information, outside of our formal application evaluation process. After carefully reviewing our course requirements we encourage you to use your best judgement in deciding whether to apply with your coursework completed to date and planned prior to your desired medical school matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Must be completed within 10 years of application date
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Secondary applications are sent to most U.S. citizens and permanent residents who submit a verified AMCAS application. In deciding whether to return secondary materials, applicants are reminded that the last entering class had an average undergraduate cumulative GPA of 3.8 and an average composite MCAT at the 91st percentile nationally.  There was a wide range around the academic metrics.  Factors assessed by the committee to rate all completed applications include: preparedness to study medicine, life experiences, meaningfulness of direct patient contact experiences, community service, leadership, teaching experiences and quality of letters of recommendation. Applicants with the highest ratings are invited for an interview. Applicants' files are reviewed without regard to race, creed, sex, national origin, age, or disability.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants should have a variety of experiences that afford them a clear understanding of the patient-physician relationship and the healthcare field. These experiences may include shadowing, volunteering, paid clinical work among others.
